sliderModel.description: Users set each trait from 0–100%. Values do not need to add up to 100. At runtime, non-zero values are normalized into effective selection weights.

examples: Béa is checking which option actually makes sense.
Béa is narrowing down the strongest options.

funny.description: Dog puns, self-deprecation, tiny-leg humor and playful absurdity.

sassy.description: Dry and mildly judgmental about routes, options or situations — never the user.
examples: Some of these recommendations have been eliminated on principle.
Béa is comparing the options. Some have disappointed her.

encouraging.description: Warm, supportive and upbeat without becoming overly cheery.
examples: The good stuff is coming together.

curious.description: Inquisitive, detail-oriented and easily intrigued by unusual places or little discoveries.
examples: Béa found a side street and now has questions.
There is something interesting over there. Béa would like to investigate.

adventurous.description: Excited by detours, hidden gems and trying something less obvious.
examples: The sensible option is good. The weird little place down the street is interesting.
Béa has spotted a detour. Naturally, she wants to know where it goes.
Three transfers. Béa has seen enough.
A seven-minute delay. Civilization may never recover.
It’ll work out. Probably. Béa is not concerned.
Béa is checking. No need for theatrics. Yet.

balanced.description: The default Béa: useful, funny, a little sassy, occasionally encouraging.

helpful.description: Clear and practical with very little personality commentary.

funny.description: More jokes, dog logic and self-deprecation.

sassy.description: Dry, sarcastic Béa with enough helpfulness to stay useful.

quirks.description: These are recurring Béa motifs, not user-controlled personality sliders. They may appear occasionally across compatible tones.
quirks.frequencyRule: Use quirks sparingly; avoid repeating the same motif within the last 5 Béa comments.

selectionRules: Determine the task/action context first: run, dig, think, ball, bone, empty state, etc.
Use the user's selected preset or custom intensities.
Normalize non-zero slider values into effective probabilities at runtime.
Choose a trait according to normalized weights, then choose a compatible line for the current action/state.
Avoid repeating any of the last 5 shown lines.
Avoid repeating the same recurring quirk within the last 5 Béa comments.
Do not rotate loading copy more often than every 4.2 seconds.
Ball and bone are rare Easter eggs, not normal loading behavior.
Sassy and Dramatic comments may tease the situation, route, result or Béa herself; never insult the user.
Errors, payments, security, destructive actions and safety-critical information always use clear non-joking copy.
